Compliance-as-code ends audit theater, the argument in one line. One framework-agnostic control register maps to SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS 4.0 and DORA simultaneously.
Failing-control workflows matter more than dashboards, findings need owners and dates.
DORA's third-party oversight is a data problem; treat the register as a governed product.
Where this goes wrong in practice

Applied carelessly, compliance-as-code ends audit theater breaks the same way every time, product-first thinking, tools purchased faster than architecture is decided, so coverage overlaps in some places and leaks in others while the estate grows more complex, not safer.

Against compliance-as-code ends audit theater, the strongest counter-case is worth naming: the architecture-first thesis can drift into analysis paralysis while the estate keeps growing. Zero-trust lands in order of blast radius, not in order of elegance.
The practice, as we run it

In delivery, compliance-as-code ends audit theater becomes a specific discipline: security here is architecture, not product sprawl, identity-first controls, segmented networks, and telemetry your SOC can act on the same hour. Every program in the Cyber & Zero-Trust domain carries the same obligations, a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
A value assessment prices the delta in your estate before anything is signed: compliance-as-code ends audit theater, measured against your baseline, in two weeks.
